summary: Sturgeon Bay Canal Light, a steel tower at the canal's north entrance, was built in 1898-99, rebuilt in 1903 after its design failed in the wind, and is now a Coast Guard aid.

lens.note: Disputed. Third order in the Lighthouse Board's 1899 report and LighthouseFriends; second order, eight panels, in the nomination's HAER form and the USLHS place record (see notes).

corrections.why: The 1898 year is the station establishment and the tower's completion (3 October 1898). The Board reported the canal light established 17 March 1899; the 1898 lights at the canal were the southeast entrance light and a beacon.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Tower completed 3 October 1898 (Board report); light first shown 17 March 1899 (Board report and LighthouseFriends); the nomination says constructed 1899. The 1898 dates in the USLHS record are the station's establishment and tower completion.

Not reconciled. The 1899 Board report and LighthouseFriends say third order; the nomination's HAER form and the USLHS place record say second order. The story follows the 1899 report; the editor should check a 1899 or 1903 Board report or the Coast Guard light list.

notes_for_editor: Record items not carried into facts: characteristic 'Fl R 10s' is not supported by any source read (LighthouseFriends says the 1899 light showed alternating red and white flashes); please check the Coast Guard light list. Range 14.8 nm is not supported by any source read (LighthouseFriends gives 18.5 miles, unit unstated). Lens order: the record's 3 follows the 1899 Board report and LighthouseFriends; the nomination and the USLHS place record say second order (see resolved_conflicts). Staffing: USLHS says automated 1972; LighthouseFriends says the Canal Station is staffed by the Coast Guard today; both are cited, neither settled. Access: the record says public; LighthouseFriends says grounds open, tower closed; facts say limited. The Dreadnaught date (27 October 1887) is inferred: the LSS entry sits under the season 1887-88 in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1888. The Nequette date (19 September 1888) is inferred the same way from the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1889. Two different Canal Stations appear: the Life-Saving Service station (keeper William Nequette; surfmen) and the lighthouse's Canal Station (LighthouseFriends's name for the light's keepers). The roster and LighthouseFriends disagree on several starts: Chapman head keeper 1886 (LighthouseFriends) versus 1899 (roster); Charles Bavry first assistant from 1896 (LighthouseFriends) versus 1899 (roster); Walter S. Lockhart 1897 (LighthouseFriends) versus 1899 (roster). LighthouseFriends-only lines carry no person slug. Conrad A. Stram (roster head keeper 1927-1933) is also named by LighthouseFriends on the Peshtigo Reef page as captain of that light vessel 1908-1913; no link is made because the link is not in the Sturgeon sources. The NRHP listing year 1984 in the record is not visible in the HAER form read here. The Board report's pierhead and southeast-entrance lights are separate structures. No newspaper search was made for this station. The roster names are archive names and are printed as the archive prints them. Persons' private details are limited to what LighthouseFriends prints about keepers whose service ended before 1960. Checked this pass: the USLHS place record gives CURRENT optic THIRD ORDER and ORIGINAL optic SECOND ORDER; the story now says so. LighthouseFriends gives Charles Bavry as first assistant from 1896 (keeper list) against the roster's 1899; the story states both. The 1888 and 1889 Life-Saving Service entries were read on the scanned text: the Dreadnaught entry is 'October 27' within the 1887-88 season (year inferred from the report's season), the Nequette entry 'September 19' within 1888-89. The keeper stints were counted from the place record: 44. The 1900 paint story and the Chapman 1933 accident follow LighthouseFriends; the tug captain is not named in the story. The 2016 demolition comment is LighthouseFriends's account of a Coast Guard notice; the Coast Guard notice itself was not read. Wording pass: about 15 sentences were reworded where they followed LighthouseFriends, NRHP or USLHS wording closely; the two LighthouseFriends quotations ('killed in a tragic accident', 'remains staffed by the Coast Guard') were turned into paraphrase.
